items.q: The mechanism chain for pressure natriuresis continued on this page runs in which order?
opts: ↑ CO → ↑ RBF → ↓ reabsorption from PCT → ↑ RIHP → ↑ medullary blood flow → ↑ Na+ & H2O excretion
↑ CO → ↓ RBF → ↑ reabsorption from PCT → ↓ medullary blood flow
↑ CO → ↑ reabsorption from PCT → ↓ RIHP → ↑ Na+ excretion
items.exp: The printed arrows are: ↑ CO → ↑ RBF → ↓ reabsorption from PCT → ↑ RIHP → ↑ medullary blood flow, which then feeds down to ↑ Na+ & H2O excretion. (Book p739)

items.q: Every step below appears in this page's pressure-natriuresis chain EXCEPT:
items.exp: The chain lists only cardiac output, RBF, PCT reabsorption, RIHP, medullary blood flow and the resulting Na+ and water excretion; aldosterone is not part of it. (Book p739)

items.q: Fill up: In the chain, the rise in medullary blood flow is immediately followed by increased excretion of ______.
items.exp: The terminal arrow of the flowchart points to ↑ Na+ & H2O excretion. (Book p739)

items.q: Compared with the filtration-fraction chain on p738, the pressure-natriuresis chain on this page moves renal interstitial hydrostatic pressure in the opposite direction.
opts: True — a raised filtration fraction lowers RIHP here while pressure natriuresis raises it
False — both chains show RIHP rising
False — both chains show RIHP falling
True — and in both chains the final effect is increased PCT reabsorption
items.exp: p738: ↑FF → ↑peritubular capillary OP → fluid taken from the interstitium → ↓RIHP → ↑PCT reabsorption. p739: ↑CO → ↑RBF → ↓PCT reabsorption → ↑RIHP → ↑medullary blood flow. The RIHP arrows point opposite ways, and the reabsorption arrows also oppose. (Book p739)
